embeds.title: HOW PSBL SCORING WORKS
embeds.description: PSBL scoring prices every play at what it's worth in runs, using the linear weights FanGraphs publishes, at 10 points per run. A hitter earns the run value of what he does, and the pitcher pays the same price from the other side. The values match FanGraphs' figures for every season from 2021 to 2026, and the reasons are below.

fields.name: HITTERS
fields.value:
Every At-Bat **−1**
Hit **+5.6**
Double **+3** more • Triple **+5.7** more
Home Run **+9.4** more
Walk **+3.1** • Hit by Pitch **+3.3**
Stolen Base **+2** • Caught Stealing **−4.1**

fields.name: PITCHERS
fields.value:
Inning Pitched **+6** (+2 per out)
Strikeout **+2**
Hit Allowed **−2.6**
Home Run Allowed **−11.4** more
Walk **−3.1** • Hit Batter **−3.3**
Save **+6** • Hold **+4**

fields.name: **━━━ HITTING ━━━**
fields.value:
**Priced in runs.** With the at-bat counted, a single nets **+4.6**, a double **+7.6**, a triple **+10.3** and a home run **+14**, and an out costs **1**. That's what each is worth in runs: a home run is about three singles, and a walk about two-thirds of one.

**No runs or RBI.** They depend on where a hitter bats and who's on base, and the hits behind them already count. A strikeout is an out like any other; the difference in runs is a tenth of a point.

**Steals:** a steal adds about 0.2 runs and getting caught costs about 0.4, so a runner has to succeed about twice for every time he's caught to come out ahead.

fields.name: **━━━ PITCHING ━━━**
fields.value:
**What a pitcher controls counts in full.** Strikeouts, walks and home runs are mostly his own doing. Whether a ball in play falls for a hit depends a lot on the defense, the park and luck, so a hit allowed costs half its run value. Tested on every starter from 2021 to 2026, that mix matched a season's runs allowed almost as well as charging hits in full, and it predicted the next season's runs allowed better than a pitcher's actual runs allowed did.

**No wins, losses or earned runs.** The offense, the bullpen and the scorer decide too much of them.

fields.name: **━━━ INNINGS AND RELIEVERS ━━━**
fields.value:
**The inning (+6) is the one number that isn't a run value.** It sets what a start is worth, so the five SP slots carry their share of the lineup: about **28%** of the value above replacement, the same as their share of the 18 slots.

**Saves (+6) and holds (+4)** pay relievers for pitching in the biggest spots. At these values the best closer in each season from 2021 to 2026 ranked between the 9th and 27th best starter: worth a roster spot, but not worth more than an ace.

fields.name: WHAT A GAME CAN LOOK LIKE
fields.value:
Homer and a single in 4 at-bats → **+16.6**
2 singles and a walk in 4 at-bats → **+10.3**
0 for 4 → **−4**
7 IP, 4 H, 1 BB, 10 K → **+48.5**
6 IP, 5 H (a homer), 2 BB, 7 K → **+19.4**
3 IP, 8 H (2 homers), 2 BB, 2 K → **−27.8**
Closer: 1 IP, 2 K, save → **+16**
Setup man: 1 IP, 1 H, 1 K, hold → **+9.4**

fields.name: **━━━ WHAT ISN'T SCORED ━━━**
fields.value:
**Runs and RBI:** the hits behind them already count.
**Wins, losses and earned runs:** the offense, the bullpen and the defense decide too much of them.
**Quality starts, complete games, shutouts and no-hitters:** innings, strikeouts and hits already reward them.
**Blown saves:** the hits and walks behind them already cost the pitcher, and a closer's blown-save rate doesn't carry over from one season to the next.

fields.name: **━━━ FOR YOUR ROSTER ━━━**
fields.value: From 2021 to 2026 a hitter in a league's lineup averaged about **5.5 points a game** and a starter about **20 points a start**. The best seasons ran about 1,300 to 1,570 for a hitter, 890 to 980 for a starter and 580 to 700 for a reliever. Hitters top the point totals because they play every day, so draft by value, not by raw points.
